kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The report provides an accurate description of the event.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Is it possible to get an accurate prediction of the weather?
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We need accurate data before we can make a final decision.

kayitlar.explanation: Showing courage; brave.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It was a courageous decision to stand up for what she believed in.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The firemen were honored for their courageous actions during the fire.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He is a courageous individual who has faced many difficulties.

kayitlar.explanation: How likely something is to happen.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: a high/strong probability of.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: There is a high probability that it will rain this afternoon.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The doctors said there was a strong probability of a full recovery.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The probability of winning the lottery is extremely low.

kayitlar.explanation: The largest part of a group of people or things.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The vast majority of students passed the exam successfully.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The government has the support of the majority of the population.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: In the majority of cases, the treatment is very effective.

kayitlar.explanation: Worth doing; that makes you happy because you think it is useful or important.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Teaching can be a very rewarding career if you love children.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Volunteering at the hospital was a deeply rewarding experience for him.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The project was difficult, but the final result was very rewarding.

kayitlar.explanation: A situation where there is not enough of something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Many countries are facing a severe shortage of clean water.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The food shortage was caused by the long period of drought.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: There is an acute shortage of skilled workers in the industry.

kayitlar.explanation: Long or longer than usual.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The region suffered from an extended drought for several years.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: They decided to take an extended holiday in Australia.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He will be away for an extended period of time for his research.

kayitlar.explanation: Causing a lot of damage and suffering.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The failure of the dam had catastrophic consequences for the town.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: A sudden economic collapse could be catastrophic for the country.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The war had a catastrophic effect on the lives of millions.

kayitlar.explanation: The state of suffering or dying because there is no food.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Millions of people are at risk of starvation in the region.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The aid workers are trying to prevent mass starvation in the camps.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: They died of starvation after being lost in the desert for weeks.

kayitlar.explanation: To damage something or make it weaker.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Lack of sleep can significantly impair your ability to drive safely.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Alcohol consumption can impair your judgment and reaction time.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The disease began to impair his vision and hearing over time.

kayitlar.explanation: Damaged or not functioning correctly.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He has impaired hearing and needs a special device to listen.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The drug can cause impaired coordination and balance.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Visually impaired students use Braille to read their textbooks.

kayitlar.explanation: Things such as food and medicines that are needed by a group of people.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The planes dropped food supplies to the isolated villages.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We need to make sure we have enough medical supplies for the trip.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The city's water supplies are running dangerously low.

kayitlar.explanation: To make something less unpleasant, difficult or painful.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to ease the pain/suffering.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The medicine helped to ease the sharp pain in his back.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The government is introducing new measures to ease the traffic problem.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Talks between the two sides have helped to ease the tension.

kayitlar.explanation: Something that can be dangerous or cause problems.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: hazard to sb/sth; fire/safety/health hazard.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Piles of dry leaves can be a serious fire hazard in the summer.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The chemical waste represents a major health hazard to local people.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Ice on the roads is a significant hazard for drivers in the winter.

kayitlar.explanation: Involving risk or danger, especially to somebody's health or safety.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The transport of hazardous chemicals is strictly regulated by law.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Working in a coal mine can be a very hazardous occupation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The mountains can be extremely hazardous in bad weather conditions.

kayitlar.explanation: To happen again or a number of times.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The same problem seems to recur every time we start the program.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: If the symptoms recur, you should see your doctor immediately.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: History has a strange tendency to recur in different forms.

kayitlar.explanation: Very large, heavy and solid.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The storm caused massive damage to the coastal towns.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The company has seen a massive increase in its profits this year.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He suffered a massive heart attack and was rushed to the hospital.

kayitlar.explanation: Things that limit or restrict something, or your freedom to do something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Financial constraints make it difficult to hire more staff at the moment.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The project was finished on time despite many technical constraints.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We need to work within the legal constraints imposed by the government.

kayitlar.explanation: Very poor; without enough money to live comfortably.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Many people live in impoverished conditions in the inner city.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The government is trying to provide more aid to impoverished regions.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The war left the country's economy completely impoverished.

kayitlar.explanation: Easily broken or damaged.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Be careful with those glasses; they are extremely fragile.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The peace agreement between the two countries is still very fragile.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The ecosystem in the desert is very fragile and easily disrupted.

kayitlar.explanation: The process of becoming worse.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: There has been a serious deterioration in his health recently.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We are seeing a gradual deterioration of the historic city walls.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The report warns of a deterioration in relations between the two nations.

kayitlar.explanation: To become worse.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The weather began to deteriorate as the storm approached the coast.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she was moved to intensive care.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Relations between the two companies have deteriorated in recent months.

kayitlar.explanation: The state of being unable to pay your debts.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The company was forced into bankruptcy after its latest project failed.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Many small businesses are facing bankruptcy due to the economic crisis.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He managed to avoid bankruptcy by selling his house and assets.

kayitlar.explanation: Unable to pay what you owe.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The firm went bankrupt after just two years of operating.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The country is almost bankrupt and needs an urgent international loan.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He was declared bankrupt by the court last month.

kayitlar.explanation: The process of something being damaged or made worse.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Environmental degradation is a major threat to wildlife in the area.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The report highlights the social degradation in poor urban neighborhoods.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Soil degradation is making it harder for farmers to grow crops.

kayitlar.explanation: To become or to make something become smaller or less important.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Our resources are diminishing rapidly, and we need to find more.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The threat of war has diminished significantly in recent weeks.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The manager's authority was diminished by his poor decisions.

kayitlar.explanation: Having little or no rain; very dry.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The region has an arid climate with very little vegetation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The desert is a vast and arid landscape where few things can survive.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Farmers struggle to grow crops on the arid land without irrigation.

kayitlar.explanation: A person or thing that is likely to cause harm; a threat.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: the menace of sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Pollution is a growing menace to the health of city residents.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He spoke with a voice that was full of menace and anger.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The menace of nuclear war hung over the world for many years.

kayitlar.explanation: Most important or famous; in the first place.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: one of the foremost causes of sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She is one of the foremost experts in the field of genetics.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Safety is our foremost concern when designing new products.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The study was published in the world's foremost medical journal.

kayitlar.explanation: Equal in value, amount, meaning, importance, etc.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: to be equivalent to.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Eight kilometers is roughly equivalent to five miles.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The new law is equivalent to a ban on all smoking in public.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She earned the equivalent of $50,000 a year in her last job.

kayitlar.explanation: Official actions that are done in order to achieve a particular goal.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: take (drastic/tough/extreme) measures (to do sth/against sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The government is taking drastic measures to reduce unemployment.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: New safety measures have been introduced at the airport.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We must take immediate measures to protect the environment.

kayitlar.explanation: A connection between people or things.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: an association between A and B.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Researchers found a strong association between lack of sleep and memory loss.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: His long association with the university began when he was a student.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: There is no direct association between the two different chemical reactions.

kayitlar.explanation: Connected with something else.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: to be associated with sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: There are several health risks associated with a high-sugar diet.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He no longer wants to be associated with that political group.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The gene is believed to be associated with the early onset of the disease.

kayitlar.explanation: The fact of being in a particular place.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: presence X absence of sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The presence of security cameras helps to prevent crime in the area.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Her quiet presence in the room made everyone feel much calmer.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Tests confirmed the presence of a rare virus in the blood samples.

kayitlar.explanation: The fact of somebody/something not being there.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: In the absence of any evidence, the police had to release the suspect.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: His long absence from work caused some problems for the team.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Plants cannot grow properly in the absolute absence of sunlight.

kayitlar.explanation: Happening or developing steadily in stages.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: progressive decline/reduction in sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The patient showed a progressive loss of memory over several months.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The company is known for its progressive approach to employee benefits.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: A progressive reduction in costs is needed to save the factory.

kayitlar.explanation: Necessary or essential in order for something to succeed or exist.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The vitamins in fruits are vital for a healthy immune system.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: It is vital to follow the safety instructions exactly as they are written.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The heart plays a vital role in pumping blood throughout the body.

kayitlar.explanation: To become smaller, fewer, or weaker; to refuse politely.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Support for the new policy has declined significantly in recent weeks.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The number of rare birds in the forest is continuing to decline.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He declined the invitation to the party because he was too busy.

kayitlar.explanation: Slightly; not in a severe or strong way.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: I was mildly surprised to hear that she had already left the city.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He spoke mildly to the children so as not to frighten them.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The doctor described the patient's symptoms as only mildly concerning.

kayitlar.explanation: Almost or very nearly.
kayitlar.note:
Adverb.
Kullanım: virtually every mental symptom.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It is virtually impossible to finish all this work in just one day.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Virtually every student in the class passed the final exam.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The two paintings look virtually identical to the untrained eye.

kayitlar.explanation: The process of becoming worse.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: A rapid deterioration in the weather forced us to cancel the hike.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The report highlights the serious deterioration of the city's old buildings.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Doctors are monitoring her for any signs of physical deterioration.

kayitlar.explanation: To happen because of something else.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Most car accidents result from human error or speeding.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The current economic problems result from a combination of factors.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Health issues often result from a lack of physical activity.
kayitlar.synonyms: stem from, arise from, come from

kayitlar.explanation: To get something, especially by making an effort.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: You need to obtain a permit before you can start building.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Further information about the course can be obtained from the library.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He managed to obtain a copy of the report through a friend.

kayitlar.explanation: To make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The government is introducing new laws to tackle the problem of crime.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We need to tackle these issues before they become even more serious.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: I decided to tackle the housework early so I could rest in the afternoon.

kayitlar.explanation: To continue to do something despite difficulties; to continue to exist.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to persist (in doing sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: If the symptoms persist for more than three days, see a doctor.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She persisted in her search for the truth despite many obstacles.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The cold weather is expected to persist throughout the week.

kayitlar.explanation: Continuing for a long time; determined to do something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He has a persistent cough that hasn't gone away for weeks.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Small businesses face persistent challenges in the current market.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She is a very persistent salesman and never gives up easily.

kayitlar.explanation: The quality of continuing to try to do something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Her persistence finally paid off when she got the job of her dreams.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The persistence of the disease in the region is a major concern.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Success in research requires a great deal of patience and persistence.

kayitlar.explanation: To make something continue at the same level or standard.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to maintain good health/standards.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It is important to maintain a healthy diet and exercise regularly.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The school works hard to maintain high standards of education.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: You must maintain your car properly to ensure it lasts a long time.
kayitlar.antonyms: abandon, give up, neglect, let go

kayitlar.explanation: Only; completely.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She chose the dress purely because she liked the color.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The decision was based purely on financial considerations.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: His interest in the project is purely professional, not personal.

kayitlar.explanation: To make a person or animal healthy again after an illness.
kayitlar.note:
Noun/Verb.
Kullanım: a cure for sth; to cure sb/sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Scientists are working hard to find a cure for cancer.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The new antibiotic managed to cure the infection very quickly.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Rest and plenty of fluids will usually cure a common cold.

kayitlar.explanation: Being an essential part of something.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: an integral part of sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Technology has become an integral part of our daily lives.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Trust is an integral part of any successful relationship.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Practical experience is an integral component of the training course.

kayitlar.explanation: An important or typical part of something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The most striking feature of the building is its giant glass dome.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The new model of the phone has several impressive safety features.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Teamwork is a significant feature of the company's culture.

kayitlar.explanation: The beginning of something, especially something unpleasant.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: the onset of sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The drugs can help to delay the onset of the disease.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: People should be prepared for the sudden onset of winter weather.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The onset of the financial crisis caught many companies by surprise.

kayitlar.explanation: To help somebody to do something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The new software is designed to assist teachers in the classroom.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We are looking for volunteers to assist with the local charity event.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He was asked to assist the police with their ongoing investigations.

kayitlar.explanation: That you are born with.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She has an inborn talent for music and can play several instruments.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Scientists are studying which human behaviors are inborn and which are learned.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The child seems to have an inborn sense of curiosity about nature.

kayitlar.explanation: Especially; more than usual.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: I found the last chapter of the book to be particularly interesting.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The weather has been particularly cold for this time of year.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She is particularly fond of classical music and attends many concerts.

kayitlar.explanation: An act of trying to do something, especially something difficult.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: in an attempt to do sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: They made an attempt to climb the mountain, but the weather was too bad.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He failed his first attempt at the driving test but passed the second time.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The government launched a new program in an attempt to reduce unemployment.

kayitlar.explanation: To move forward; to improve or develop.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: As the day progressed, the temperature began to rise steadily.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The project is progressing well and should be finished on time.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Medical researchers are watching how the disease progresses in patients.

kayitlar.explanation: Connected with literature.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She is a well-known figure in London's literary circles.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The prize is awarded annually for outstanding literary merit.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He has published several literary essays in prestigious journals.

kayitlar.explanation: People who live at the same time as someone else, or are about the same age.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Einstein was much more advanced than most of his contemporaries.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She was a contemporary of many famous poets of the nineteenth century.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: His work was not fully appreciated by his contemporaries during his lifetime.
kayitlar.synonyms: peers, colleagues of the same era

kayitlar.explanation: Used to describe people who belong to the same group or class or who share a situation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He greeted his fellow graduates with a short but inspiring speech.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We must show compassion for our fellow citizens in times of crisis.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She is highly respected by her fellow workers for her dedication.

kayitlar.explanation: Connected with making money by starting or running businesses.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The university encourages students to develop their entrepreneurial skills.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He has a strong entrepreneurial spirit and has started several companies.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The city is famous for its entrepreneurial culture and tech startups.

kayitlar.explanation: The quality of being famous and respected, especially in a profession.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He achieved great eminence as a world-renowned heart surgeon.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She rose to eminence in the field of international law.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: His academic eminence makes him a highly respected figure at the college.

kayitlar.explanation: Great skill or intelligence.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The pianist amazed the audience with the technical brilliance of her performance.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Everyone admired the brilliance of his scientific discoveries.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The young student showed early signs of mathematical brilliance.

kayitlar.explanation: The time in a person's life when they develop from a child into an adult.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Adolescence can be a difficult period for both children and their parents.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She spent much of her adolescence living in a small rural town.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The book explores the emotional changes that occur during adolescence.

kayitlar.explanation: Far away from where other people live.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: They live in a remote mountain village that is difficult to reach.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The research station is located in a remote part of the Antarctic.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: There is a remote possibility that the flight will be delayed.

kayitlar.explanation: Happy and satisfied with your life.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She gave a contented sigh as she sat down with her favorite book.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He led a very quiet and contented life in the country.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The baby looked very contented after her afternoon nap.

kayitlar.explanation: In a way that shows someone is happy or satisfied.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The cat sat contentedly by the fire, purring softly.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He smiled contentedly as he watched his children playing in the garden.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: They spent the evening talking contentedly about their future plans.

kayitlar.explanation: Controlled or influenced mainly by people who have university degrees.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The industry has become increasingly graduate-dominated in recent years.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Entry into this graduate-dominated profession is very competitive.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The company's management team is heavily graduate-dominated.

kayitlar.explanation: Pleasantly new or different.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It made a refreshing change to hear some good news for once.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She has a refreshing approach to problem-solving in the office.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: His honesty was quite refreshing after all the lies we had heard.

kayitlar.explanation: Nervous or embarrassed about your appearance or what other people think of you.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He was very self-conscious about his height when he was a teenager.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She felt self-conscious standing in front of such a large audience.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Don't be so self-conscious; nobody is looking at you.

kayitlar.explanation: To give somebody what they allow or have asked for.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The court decided to grant him permission to appeal.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The experience granted her a new perspective on life.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: This software grants exclusive access to certain restricted files.

kayitlar.explanation: A feeling of great respect sometimes mixed with fear.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: to be in awe of sb/sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: They were in awe of the magnificent mountain range.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He spoke in a voice that was full of awe and admiration.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The young actors were in complete awe of the veteran director.

kayitlar.explanation: To help someone to understand more about the world and different ideas.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Travel is often said to broaden the mind by exposing us to new cultures.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Reading books on different subjects will definitely broaden your mind.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The university course really broadened his mind about global issues.
kayitlar.synonyms: expand the mind, open the mind, widen one's horizons
kayitlar.antonyms: narrow the mind, close the mind

kayitlar.explanation: Very pleasant or enjoyable.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: We spent a delightful afternoon walking along the river bank.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Thank you for the delightful meal; we had a wonderful time.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The hotel was delightful, with beautiful rooms and friendly staff.

kayitlar.explanation: The freedom to live as you wish or go where you want.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: a place of liberty.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The constitution guarantees the basic liberties of all citizens.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: They fought bravely for their country's national liberty.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The internet was once seen as a place of absolute liberty and freedom.

kayitlar.explanation: The policy or practice of examining books, films, etc. and removing offensive parts.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The government was criticized for its strict internet censorship.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The report highlights the growing censorship of the press in that country.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Many artists are fighting against any form of artistic censorship.

kayitlar.explanation: To examine books, films, etc. and remove parts considered offensive.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The movie was heavily censored before it was shown on television.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Authorities often censor news reports during times of political unrest.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: They decided to censor certain scenes that they thought were inappropriate.

kayitlar.explanation: To forbid something officially.
kayitlar.note:
Verb/Noun.
Kullanım: a ban on sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The government has decided to ban smoking in public parks.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: There is a total ban on the use of mobile phones during exams.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He was banned from driving for six months after the accident.

kayitlar.explanation: A law or a set of laws passed by a parliament.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: New legislation will be introduced to control water pollution.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The parliament passed landmark legislation to protect children's rights.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Environmental legislation has helped to reduce industrial emissions.

kayitlar.explanation: To introduce a new law, rule, or tax; to force somebody to accept something.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to impose sth on/upon sb/sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The council has decided to impose a ban on parking here.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: New taxes were imposed on luxury goods last month.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: I don't want to impose my personal views on you.

kayitlar.explanation: The act of introducing a new law, rule, tax, etc.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The imposition of strict rules was necessary to ensure safety.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: They protested against the imposition of higher tuition fees.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The imposition of censorship limited the freedom of speech.

kayitlar.explanation: To stop something from being done by law or rules.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: prohibit sb from doing sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The law prohibits the sale of alcohol to minors.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Visitors are prohibited from taking photos inside the museum.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The new regulations prohibit the use of certain pesticides.

kayitlar.explanation: The act of stopping something from being done by a law or rule.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: the prohibition of sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The report calls for a global prohibition of child labor.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The prohibition of drugs remains a major challenge for the police.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: They strictly follow the prohibition against eating in the lab.

kayitlar.explanation: To make sure that people obey a particular law or rule.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to enforce sth (on/against sb).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It is the job of the police to enforce the law.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The school has strict rules that are firmly enforced.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: New safety regulations will be strictly enforced from now on.

kayitlar.explanation: A possible effect or result of an action or a decision.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: implication of sth for sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The development of AI has serious implications for the future of work.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The research has significant implications for how we treat the disease.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We need to consider the financial implications of this decision.

kayitlar.explanation: To think about a problem and decide how you are going to deal with it.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The government must address the problem of poverty immediately.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We need to address these issues before they get out of hand.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: His speech failed to address the concerns of the local people.

kayitlar.explanation: To show that somebody/something is right or reasonable.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: How can you justify spending so much money on a car?
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The results justify the hard work we put in.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He tried to justify his behavior with various excuses.

kayitlar.explanation: A good reason why something exists or is done.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: There is no justification for such extreme violence.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: What is the justification for this new tax increase?
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The report provides a detailed justification for the changes.

kayitlar.explanation: An idea, a belief or an understanding of something.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: notion of sth / notion that... / accept/challenge/reject a notion.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The traditional notion of family has changed in recent years.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: I reject the notion that success is only about money.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He challenged the notion that we are solely responsible for the issue.

kayitlar.explanation: That is possible and likely to be achieved.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It is no longer feasible to continue with the current plan.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The committee decided that the project was not financially feasible.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We are looking for a feasible solution to the traffic problem.

kayitlar.explanation: Feeling very upset, anxious or worried.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The news left her feeling very distressed and confused.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: They received a distressed phone call from their son late at night.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The charity helps distressed families in war-torn areas.

kayitlar.explanation: The act of using something especially for a practical purpose.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The effective utilization of energy is a key goal for the city.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We must maximize the utilization of our existing resources.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The study looks at the utilization of technology in schools.

kayitlar.explanation: The ability to make sensible decisions based on experience.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: have the wisdom to do sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She has gained much wisdom through her years of travel.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: I hope you have the wisdom to make the right choice.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Common wisdom says that you should save money for the future.

kayitlar.explanation: In order to help or please someone; because of the interest of something.
kayitlar.note:
Idiom.
Kullanım: for the sake of sth/doing sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: They stayed together for the sake of their children.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Let's not argue for the sake of argument.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He gave up smoking for the sake of his health.
kayitlar.synonyms: for the benefit of, in the interest of

kayitlar.explanation: A substance that controls the effects of a poison; anything that takes away an unpleasant feeling.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Laughter is a great antidote to stress and anxiety.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Doctors administered the antidote as soon as he arrived.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: A walk in the fresh air was the perfect antidote to his bad mood.

kayitlar.explanation: Needing or depending on somebody/something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The company is heavily reliant on export sales.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We are becoming increasingly reliant on technology for everything.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: As he got older, he became more reliant on his children for help.

kayitlar.explanation: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: integrity of a medium.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She is a woman of great integrity who always tells the truth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The investigation questioned the professional integrity of the manager.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We must protect the integrity of the data collected during research.

kayitlar.explanation: Limited in size, amount, or what is allowed.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Entrance to the building is restricted to authorized personnel.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The use of certain chemicals is strictly restricted by law.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: I am on a restricted diet for health reasons.

kayitlar.explanation: Difficult to understand or explain.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The police are investigating the mysterious disappearance of the hiker.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The house had a mysterious atmosphere that made us nervous.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Scientists are trying to explain the mysterious lights in the sky.

kayitlar.explanation: Something that is difficult to understand or explain.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: to solve/uncover/unravel/explain a mystery.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The cause of the fire remains a complete mystery to investigators.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The detective spent years trying to uncover the mystery of the theft.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The vast universe is full of mysteries yet to be discovered.

kayitlar.explanation: To become impossible to see.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The sun disappeared behind a thick cloud and it started to rain.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Traditional ways of life are slowly disappearing in modern cities.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Her keys seem to have disappeared from the table.

kayitlar.explanation: The fact of somebody/something becoming impossible to see or find.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: disappearance of sb/sth (from sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The sudden disappearance of the plane remains unexplained.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Police are still searching for clues about her disappearance.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We are concerned about the disappearance of rare plants in the forest.

kayitlar.explanation: That you would like to have yourself; very good.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He has the enviable reputation of being the best chef in town.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The company is in an enviable position with high profits.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She has an enviable ability to stay calm under pressure.

kayitlar.explanation: Wanting to be in the same situation as somebody else.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: to be envious (of sb/sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He was deeply envious of his brother's success in business.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: They were envious of their neighbors' new car.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She felt a bit envious when she saw her friend's travel photos.

kayitlar.explanation: In a way that makes you want to have the same thing yourself.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She has an enviably slender figure even at her age.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The garden is enviably tidy and full of beautiful flowers.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He manages his time enviably well, always finishing early.

kayitlar.explanation: To disappear suddenly.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: vanish (without a trace/into thin air/from the face of the earth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The magician made the rabbit vanish into thin air.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: My wallet seems to have vanished from my bag.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The snow will quickly vanish when the sun comes out.

kayitlar.explanation: Easy to see or understand.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: for no apparent reason; to be apparent from sth; apparent to sb.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It was apparent from her face that she was unhappy.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The cause of the problem was not immediately apparent.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: For no apparent reason, the computer suddenly stopped working.

kayitlar.explanation: According to what you have heard or read; according to the way something appears.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Apparently, they are planning to get married next year.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He has been ill for several days, apparently with a bad cold.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Apparently, the match has been canceled due to rain.

kayitlar.explanation: To suggest something in an indirect way.
kayitlar.note:
Verb/Noun.
Kullanım: to hint (that) / hint at sth; give sb a hint.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The manager hinted that there might be staff changes soon.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He hinted at the possibility of a resignation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She gave me a helpful hint on how to solve the puzzle.

kayitlar.explanation: To look like or be similar to another person or thing.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She closely resembles her mother when she was younger.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The plant's leaves resemble a human hand.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The two situations resemble each other in many ways.
kayitlar.synonyms: look like, be similar to, mirror, echo

kayitlar.explanation: The state of being similar to another person or thing.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: bear a (striking/close/strong) resemblance to; resemblance between A and B.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: There is a striking resemblance between the two cousins.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The new building bears little resemblance to the original design.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: I can see a strong resemblance between her and her grandmother.

kayitlar.explanation: Very close to experiencing or doing something.
kayitlar.note:
Idiom.
Kullanım: to be on the verge of sth/of doing sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The company was on the verge of bankruptcy before the loan.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Scientists are on the verge of making a major breakthrough.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The species is on the verge of extinction and needs protection.

kayitlar.explanation: A strong desire or impulse to do something.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: feel/have/resist/fight/suppress an urge to do sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She felt a sudden urge to laugh during the serious meeting.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He had to fight the urge to tell his boss exactly what he thought.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Whenever he sees a beautiful landscape, he has an urge to paint it.

kayitlar.explanation: Used before a person or thing that is the only one not included in a statement.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The office was empty except for a single security guard at the desk.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The house was quiet except for the ticking of the old clock.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: I've finished all my homework except for the last math problem.

kayitlar.explanation: To refuse an offer, request, or invitation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He had to turn down the job offer because the salary was too low.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She turned down his invitation to dinner, saying she was busy.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The bank turned down their application for a loan to start a business.

kayitlar.explanation: The state of being available for somebody to use.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: at sb's disposal / at the disposal of sb.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: I am entirely at your disposal; just let me know what you need.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The company has significant financial resources at its disposal.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: A car and driver were put at the disposal of the visiting diplomat.

kayitlar.explanation: Almost or very nearly.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It is virtually impossible to find a parking space in the city center.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The two brothers look virtually identical, even though they aren't twins.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He has virtually no experience in this field of engineering.

kayitlar.explanation: To give a document, proposal, etc. to somebody in authority.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to submit sth (to sb/sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: You must submit your application form by the end of the week.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The committee asked the researchers to submit a detailed report.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He submitted his resignation to the board of directors yesterday.
kayitlar.synonyms: send in, hand in, present, turn in

kayitlar.explanation: The act of giving a document or piece of work to someone.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The deadline for the submission of essays is next Friday.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: We received over a hundred submissions for the short story competition.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The project is now ready for submission to the head office.

kayitlar.explanation: The possibility of being successful in the future.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Taking this course will greatly improve your career prospects.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The economic prospects for the next year are looking quite positive.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: There are little prospects of a quick recovery for the industry.

kayitlar.explanation: Regarding or concerning something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: As regards the cost, we will need to discuss that with the manager.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: I have no complaints as regards the quality of the service.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The company is performing well as regards its international sales.

kayitlar.explanation: A task or project, especially one that is important or difficult.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Building a new airport is a major undertaking for any city.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The research project was a complex undertaking involving three universities.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: I'm not sure if we are ready for such a risky financial undertaking.

kayitlar.explanation: To agree to do or be responsible for a task or project.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to undertake a task/project/research.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The university decided to undertake a study on the local environment.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She was willing to undertake the task despite the many challenges.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The company undertook a complete restructuring of its staff.
kayitlar.synonyms: take on, commit to, begin, engage in

kayitlar.explanation: A small part of a group that is less than half of the whole.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Only a small minority of students failed to pass the final exam.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The government must protect the rights of ethnic minorities.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: They found themselves in the minority during the vote on the new rules.

kayitlar.explanation: The act of suggesting someone for a job, award, or position.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: a nomination for sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He received a nomination for Best Actor for his role in the film.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The nomination period for the election closes at the end of the month.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Her nomination for the post was supported by many of her colleagues.

kayitlar.explanation: To suggest someone officially for a job, prize, or position.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to nominate sb (for sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: I would like to nominate Sarah for the position of team leader.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He was nominated for an Oscar for his latest documentary.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The committee will nominate three candidates for the award.

kayitlar.explanation: By good luck.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Fortunately, nobody was injured in the accident last night.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The storm was heavy, but fortunately our house was not damaged.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Fortunately, I had already finished the report before my computer crashed.

kayitlar.explanation: According to the customs or usual practices associated with a group.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It is customary to shake hands when you meet someone for the first time.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The wedding was performed with the customary ceremonies and rituals.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She arrived with her customary smile and greeted everyone warmly.

kayitlar.explanation: A person who answers a survey or a set of questions.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Most of the respondents to the survey expressed high satisfaction.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The researchers interviewed over five hundred respondents in the city.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Each respondent was asked to provide their age and occupation.

kayitlar.explanation: Very great, strong, or serious.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: intense pressure/heat/activity; at an intense rate.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The athletes were under intense pressure to win the gold medal.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The heat from the sun was so intense that they had to stay indoors.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The city is growing at an intense rate compared to last decade.

kayitlar.explanation: To behave according to the usual standards of behavior that are expected.
kayitlar.note:
Phrasal Verb.
Kullanım: conform to rules/standards.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The building must conform to all safety regulations before it opens.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Many people feel a strong pressure to conform to social standards.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He refused to conform to the traditional ways of his family.
kayitlar.synonyms: comply with, follow, adhere to, observe

kayitlar.explanation: Behavior that follows established customs or patterns.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The school uniform is intended to encourage a sense of conformity.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: They live in strict conformity with the laws of their community.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She was criticized for her lack of conformity to the rules.

kayitlar.explanation: A person who behaves like everyone else and follows rules strictly.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He is a natural conformist who never likes to stand out from the crowd.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The office environment is very conformist, with everyone dressing similarly.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: As a non-conformist, she always preferred to do things her own way.

kayitlar.explanation: Clear and easy to understand.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The teacher gave the students explicit instructions on how to do the project.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The report provides explicit evidence of the company's financial problems.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She was very explicit about what she expected from her team.

kayitlar.explanation: Suggested without being directly expressed.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: There was an implicit understanding between them that they would help each other.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Her criticism was implicit in the way she looked at the painting.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The meaning of the poem is implicit rather than clearly stated.

kayitlar.explanation: To show someone the right way or give advice.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The compass helped them guide their way through the thick forest.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Her parents guided her through the difficult process of choosing a career.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Experienced teachers guide new students during their first week.

kayitlar.explanation: To accept and act according to a law, rule, or decision.
kayitlar.note:
Phrasal Verb.
Kullanım: abide by sb's decision/rules/law.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: All members of the club must agree to abide by the rules.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: I will abide by the judge's decision, whatever it may be.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Drivers who fail to abide by the law will face heavy fines.

kayitlar.explanation: That exists or is very common at a particular time or in a particular place.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: prevalent among young children/in big cities.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The disease is more prevalent in tropical regions of the world.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: These beliefs are still prevalent among the local population.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Unemployment is unfortunately very prevalent in small industrial towns.

kayitlar.explanation: To move back or away from a place or situation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The company decided to withdraw its sponsorship of the event.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The army was ordered to withdraw from the border immediately.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She decided to withdraw from the competition due to an injury.
kayitlar.synonyms: pull back, retreat, remove, take out

kayitlar.explanation: The ideas and opinions that are thought to be normal because they are shared by most people.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: These alternative views are slowly entering mainstream politics.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The artist finally achieved mainstream success with his latest album.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Mainstream media often ignores the problems of small rural communities.

kayitlar.explanation: Very strange or unusual.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He has some bizarre habits, like sleeping with the lights on.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The movie has a very bizarre plot that is hard to follow.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: They found themselves in a bizarre situation that they couldn't explain.

kayitlar.explanation: A fact or event in nature or society, especially one that is not fully understood.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The Northern Lights are a spectacular natural phenomenon.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Social media is a relatively recent global phenomenon.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Scientists are studying the phenomenon of global warming closely.

kayitlar.explanation: To take part in something.
kayitlar.note:
Phrasal Verb.
Kullanım: to engage in sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Most of the students engage in extracurricular activities after school.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: They were engaged in a deep conversation about their future plans.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The company refused to engage in any unethical business practices.
kayitlar.synonyms: participate in, take part in, involve oneself in

kayitlar.explanation: The state of being completely involved in something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Full immersion in the local culture is the best way to learn a language.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The course offers a total immersion in the world of professional cooking.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She found peace through her immersion in her art and music.

kayitlar.explanation: To use something such as a skill, method, etc. for a particular purpose.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The builders employed traditional methods to restore the old house.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: You should employ your skills to help others in the community.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The detective employed a clever trick to catch the thief.
kayitlar.synonyms: use, apply, make use of, utilize

kayitlar.explanation: The fact of doing something together or of working with someone else towards a shared aim.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: cooperation of sb / with sb / between A and B.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The project was a success thanks to the cooperation of all team members.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: International cooperation is essential to fight against climate change.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: There was a complete lack of cooperation between the two departments.

kayitlar.explanation: Having a close and friendly relationship.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: They share an intimate friendship that has lasted for twenty years.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The restaurant has a warm and intimate atmosphere, perfect for a date.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She told her sister every intimate detail of her long journey.

kayitlar.explanation: To tell somebody secrets and personal information because you trust them.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to confide sth to sb.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She decided to confide her secrets to her best friend.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He confided that he was planning to leave the company soon.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: It's important to have someone you can confide in when you have problems.

kayitlar.explanation: A strong desire to do something, especially something that is wrong or silly.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: a (constant) compulsion (to do sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He felt a strong compulsion to check his phone every few minutes.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Gambling can become a powerful compulsion that is hard to break.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Some people have a constant compulsion to tidy their environment.

kayitlar.explanation: Difficult to stop or control.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Her compulsive spending led her into a lot of financial debt.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He is a compulsive liar and you can never trust what he says.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Compulsive overeating is often linked to high levels of stress.

kayitlar.explanation: To happen or appear for the first time in a particular place or situation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The tradition originated from an ancient ritual in the village.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Many English words actually originate from Latin or Greek.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The fire is believed to have originated in the kitchen of the building.

kayitlar.explanation: To fail to take care of somebody/something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He was accused of neglecting his duties at the hospital.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: You should not neglect your health by working too much.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The garden had been neglected for years and was full of weeds.
kayitlar.antonyms: care for, attend to, nurture, look after

kayitlar.explanation: Tending to hide your feelings, thoughts, or actions from other people.
kayitlar.note:
Adjective.
Kullanım: to be secretive (about sth).
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He is very secretive about his private life and never talks about it.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The company was very secretive about its new research project.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She became increasingly secretive as the surprise party approached.

kayitlar.explanation: The unfair, cruel, or violent treatment of somebody/something.
kayitlar.note:
Noun/Verb.
Kullanım: substance/alcohol/drug abuse; to abuse alcohol/drugs.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The report highlights the serious problem of drug abuse among youth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He was fired from his job because he began to abuse alcohol.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Child abuse is a horrific crime that must be severely punished.

kayitlar.explanation: To make something seem larger, better, worse, or more important than it really is.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to exaggerate sth/an activity.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Don't exaggerate; the journey didn't take that long!
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He tends to exaggerate his achievements to impress other people.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The newspapers often exaggerate the danger of certain situations.

kayitlar.explanation: A statement that makes something seem more than it really is.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: It is no exaggeration to say that she is the best in the world.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The story was full of exaggerations and was hard to believe.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He described the storm with a great deal of exaggeration.

kayitlar.explanation: Trying to prevent somebody from doing something by making difficulties.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: His obstructive behavior during the meeting was very frustrating.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The company was accused of being obstructive to the investigation.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: We need to identify and remove any obstructive factors to progress.

kayitlar.explanation: To block a road, passage, etc. so that nothing can go through.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The fallen tree completely obstructed the road to the village.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Protesters tried to obstruct the entrance to the building.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: You should not obstruct the police while they are doing their job.

kayitlar.explanation: The fact of blocking a road, passage, etc.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The driver was charged with obstruction of the public highway.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The surgeon removed an obstruction from the patient's artery.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The match was delayed because of an obstruction on the field.

kayitlar.explanation: To choose not to do or have something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He decided to abstain from alcohol for the rest of the month.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Ten members of the committee chose to abstain from voting.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The doctor advised him to abstain from eating fatty foods.
kayitlar.synonyms: refrain, avoid, hold back, keep off

kayitlar.explanation: To become involved in a situation in order to improve or help it.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: to intervene in sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The police had to intervene to stop the fight in the street.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The government refused to intervene in the industrial dispute.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She decided to intervene before the argument became even worse.
kayitlar.antonyms: stand aside, ignore, stay out of

kayitlar.explanation: The act of becoming involved in a situation to help it.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The sudden intervention of the bank saved the company from failure.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Medical intervention was necessary to save the patient's life.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The country called for an international intervention to end the war.

kayitlar.explanation: A physical condition caused by not having enough food or the right food.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: to suffer from / treatment for malnutrition.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Millions of children in the region suffer from severe malnutrition.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The charity provides treatment for malnutrition in poor communities.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The report highlights the link between poverty and malnutrition.

kayitlar.explanation: To develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complicated form.
kayitlar.note:
Verb.
Kullanım: sth evolves / to evolve into sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The company has evolved over the years into a multi-million dollar organization.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Scientists believe that birds evolved from small dinosaurs millions of years ago.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Language is a living thing that continues to evolve and change every day.

kayitlar.explanation: The slow and gradual development of something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Darwin's theory of evolution changed the way we understand life on Earth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The book traces the evolution of modern art from its early beginnings.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The rapid evolution of technology has revolutionized the way we communicate.

kayitlar.explanation: Used before a date to mean 'approximately'.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The ancient temple was built circa 500 BC according to archaeologists.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The manuscript dates from circa 1450 and is in excellent condition.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He was born circa 1920 in a small village in the south of Italy.

kayitlar.explanation: Frequent changes in size, amount, quality, etc.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The company is struggling to cope with sudden fluctuations in the market price.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Currency fluctuations can make it difficult for businesses to plan ahead.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Temperature fluctuations during the night are very common in the desert.

kayitlar.explanation: To change frequently in size, amount, quality, etc.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The price of oil continues to fluctuate wildly on the global market.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: His weight tends to fluctuate depending on his level of physical activity.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The number of students in the class fluctuates between twenty and thirty.

kayitlar.explanation: An official piece of paper on which a doctor writes the medicine you need.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The doctor wrote me a prescription for some antibiotics today.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: You can only get this medicine from the pharmacy with a prescription.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He misplaced his prescription and had to go back to the clinic for a new one.

kayitlar.explanation: To tell somebody to take a particular medicine or treatment.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The specialist prescribed a new course of treatment for his condition.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Doctors should be careful not to prescribe too many different drugs at once.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She was prescribed bed rest and plenty of fluids for her recovery.

kayitlar.explanation: Machines that are designed to do a particular job in the home.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The store sells a wide range of electrical appliances, from toasters to fridges.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Modern home appliances have made housework much easier and faster.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Always unplug your appliances before you leave the house for a long time.

kayitlar.explanation: An illegal act; a crime.
kayitlar.note:
Noun.
Kullanım: a criminal offense / commit offenses.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Driving without a valid license is a serious criminal offense.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He was arrested for committing a series of minor offenses in the city.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Computer security offenses have become much more common recently.

kayitlar.explanation: A person who commits a crime.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The judge decided to give the first-time offender a lighter sentence.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The police are using technology to track down dangerous offenders.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Many young offenders are sent to special centers rather than prison.

kayitlar.explanation: One of several parts of which something is made.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: Trust is a vital component of any successful relationship.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The factory produces various components for aircraft engines.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: Practical training is a key component of the overall educational program.

kayitlar.explanation: To know or say that something will happen in the future.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: No one could foresee the impact the internet would have on society.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The company failed to foresee the sudden change in consumer behavior.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: It is difficult to foresee what the economic situation will be like next year.

kayitlar.explanation: To punish somebody for breaking a rule or a law.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The team was penalized for having too many players on the field.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: You will be penalized if you do not submit your application on time.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The new law aims to penalize companies that pollute the environment.

kayitlar.explanation: In a way that continues without stopping or getting less severe.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The rain fell relentlessly all day, causing flooding in several areas.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She worked relentlessly to finish the project before the deadline.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The army pursued the enemy relentlessly across the difficult landscape.

kayitlar.explanation: To change something so that it is no longer true or accurate.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The media was accused of trying to distort the facts of the case.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Loud music can sometimes distort the sound of the singer's voice.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He intentionally distorted the truth to make himself look better.

kayitlar.explanation: To make somebody/something experience something, especially something unpleasant.
kayitlar.note:
Verb Phrase.
Kullanım: subject sb/sth to sth.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The prisoners were subjected to cruel and unusual punishment.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The new drug was subjected to a series of rigorous clinical tests.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: She didn't want to subject her family to any more unnecessary stress.
kayitlar.synonyms: exposed to, subjected to, made to experience

kayitlar.explanation: Not seeming to be based on a reason, system or plan.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The decision to close the library seemed completely arbitrary to the residents.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He made an arbitrary choice from the menu without even looking at it.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The rules of the game felt arbitrary and difficult to follow.

kayitlar.explanation: Not having a good reason.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The criticism she received from her manager was entirely unjustified.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He felt that the high price of the ticket was completely unjustified.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The use of force in that situation was considered unjustified by the court.

kayitlar.explanation: A good reason why something exists or is done.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: There is no justification for such extreme violence against civilians.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: What is the justification for this new tax increase on basic goods?
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The report provides a detailed justification for the policy changes.

kayitlar.explanation: To do something or try to achieve something over a period of time.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She decided to move to New York to pursue a career in fashion.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: Students are encouraged to pursue non-academic activities like sports.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He has been pursuing his interest in photography for many years.

kayitlar.explanation: The act of making somebody suffer something unpleasant.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The deliberate infliction of pain on animals is a serious crime.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The report condemned the infliction of harsh punishments on children.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The war resulted in the infliction of great suffering on the population.

kayitlar.explanation: The feeling of being ashamed or losing respect.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: He felt a deep sense of humiliation after he lost the match so easily.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: She couldn't bear the humiliation of having to ask for money.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The public humiliation was enough to make him resign from his post.

kayitlar.explanation: To make somebody feel ashamed or stupid and lose respect.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: I didn't mean to humiliate you in front of all your friends.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: The teacher's comments were intended to humiliate the student.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: He felt humiliated by the way his manager spoke to him yesterday.

kayitlar.explanation: To introduce a new law, rule, or test; to force somebody to accept something.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: The council has decided to impose a ban on parking here.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: New laws were imposed to control the use of dangerous chemicals.
kayitlar.exampleSentence3: The school decided to impose drug testing for all student athletes.

kayitlar.explanation: To offer to do something without being forced or paid.
kayitlar.exampleSentence1: She volunteered to help with the charity event next weekend.
kayitlar.exampleSentence2: He works as a volunteer at the local animal shelter twice a week.
